utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Good morning. Would the registrar please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Case number IT-95-9-T, the Prosecutor versus Blagoje Simic, Milan Simic, Miroslav Tadic, and Simo Zaric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The Prosecution is continuing examination-in-chief. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Examined by Mr. di Fazio: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Izetbegovic, yesterday we had reached the point where you were describing your exchange, or rather, your departure from Batajnica. You told us that you were flown to Pale, and there you met General Mladic, or encountered him. Can you pick up your story from that point and tell us of the events upon your arrival in Pale.

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When the helicopter landed, the men who were with me in the helicopter got off. I was the last to remain, and this person who was in charge of me. I heard a voice outside, saying, "Have you brought Izetbegovic?" And this one said, "Yes, we have, General." I didn't know which General he was referring to, and it was also the first time I had heard of his name. I got off. I was escorted out and taken to the general. He was wearing a general's uniform, in fact. He introduced himself to me. "I am General Mladic, he said. And I said, "Pleased to meet you." What else could I have said? He acted in a very correct, military manner. In fact, he said to me, "At ease," though I had really gone stiff out of fear, not for any other reason. Then the soldiers lined up and they left somewhere and we were left alone. We had a conversation. He asked me a few questions linked to the situation. Of course, I couldn't tell him anything, because everyone thought that I was some important figure in those events. However, I told him that I had no broader powers except for those I had acquired locally as an elected official and that I was performing my duties like any other citizen would do. He also said many other things to me, many of them I had heard for the first time, and only then did I realise what was at stake, and that was also the first time I saw so many soldiers and weapons, and many things became clear to me then. After that, UNPROFOR officers came and took me off, with an escort, and I was taken over by General Boskovic, who was then the commander of the military area of Yugoslavia. There was a colonel, there was a captain. All of them were, of course, officers of the Yugoslav People's Army at the time. When we were entering the special armoured vehicle - in fact, there were three UN armoured white vehicles - General Mladic shouted out, "Let Izetbegovic sit next to the driver." Then General Boskovic turned around and said, "No. He'll sit where I sit." I realised then that relationships between them were not quite what they should be regarding command. So I got into the armoured part of the vehicle and we headed downwards, and I was exchanged at the PTT engineering building in Sarajevo. I was taken over.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you were driven from Pale to Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With the two generals?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: One general, General Boskovic, and a colonel, also known as Cadjo, and I heard him being mentioned later on. I stayed in Sarajevo until November or December that year. I couldn't get out. I didn't know where my family was. But I later heard on the radio that he was mentioned as a commander in the siege of Sarajevo, whereas I never again heard or saw General Boskovic. He handed me over to the defence minister of Bosnia-Herzegovina, Jerko Doko. I just know that Jerko Doko said to him, "I hadn't [as interpreted] known the man before. What have you done to him? I wouldn't believe it was him." I was wearing an old, torn military uniform which was still bloodstained. I was tied with rope because the clothing we had was taken away from us for dry-cleaning. This was in Belgrade. And then they took me to the presidency, of course. They welcomed me there, that is, the people who were meant to welcome me, and from there I was taken to hospital.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell us how long you remained in Sarajevo before leaving?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I stayed in Sarajevo until the end of November, the 27th or 28th of November I think was the first time I left the town on an UNPROFOR plane.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Was Sarajevo being shelled during that time?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Throughout that time it was shelled. It was terrible. And I kept thinking to myself: Was it worse here or where I had been before? These shells were falling all over. Then there was a shortage of food and everything else. 1993 in particular was terrible. But I left, so ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I want to ask you some brief questions. They may seem obvious to you, but I need to know --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I'm sorry. The inclusion of saying "1993 in particular was terrible" may cause some confusion. What year was he released from Sarajevo? MR. DI FAZIO: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You heard Her Honour's question. You've told us, you've given evidence that you were initially arrested in April of 1992, kept in custody and so on. What year did the events you've just described occur in, namely, your release from Batajnica, the transfer to Pale and the transfer to Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It all occurred in 1992. At the end of 1992, I left to Sarajevo. But I just mentioned 1993 because I knew and I suffered because of the situation in my country, and that was quite normal, and that year was the worst perhaps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, I just want to ask you one or two brief questions that may seem unusual to you, but just answer it yes or no, if you can. Did you have any choice in being exchanged, or rather, I've used that term, in being handed over from Yugoslavian authorities into the hands of Bosnian authorities at Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand quite what you mean by "choice."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have any influence on those actions?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No influence whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just gave myself up to them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was in their hands.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. That's exactly what I --

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Don't mention it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: Mr. Izetbegovic, you left Sarajevo on the 27th or 29th, you said. Where did you go to in the plane?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I went to Zagreb, because that was where the flight went. I got off in Zagreb. I was quite free. Then I went around, looking for my family to see whether they were alive and where they were. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've told us at the beginning of your evidence of how your family had owned land in Bosanski Samac, how you had been the owner of a house in which generations of your family were raised. At the time that you were transferred -- I've fallen into it again and I apologise. At the time that you were handed over to Sarajevo Bosnian authorities, had you been given anything at all attesting to the fact of your ownership of property back in Bosanski Samac or guaranteeing your rights of property in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't receive any guarantees and I didn't ask for them either, though.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What else did you lose in Bosanski Samac apart from your house? I'm referring to possessions now, personal property.

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time we just had the house, and the children had their own household. But the things I was talking about previously, a part of that was taken in 1918, that is Pelagicevo today. We had a large estate. It used to be Zabar. And the second part of that estate in 1945.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. What I'm interested in is the situation in April of 1992. At that time, you -- I assume you owned property. You've told us you owned a house. Did you own other things; furniture, car, bank accounts, that sort of thing, located in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I had a house fully furnished, I had an apartment of 180 square metres in area in the house. In another part was a business owned by my nephew. There was furniture. I had a car, I had a foreign exchange account in the Belgradska Bank. I don't know what happened to that; I never used the money.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you've told us you weren't given any document attesting to your title in the house. Were you given any documentation attesting to property rights in other property apart from the house?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't get any certificates and I didn't ask for them. I can't accept that I have to make a request for something that is mine, and I still believe this is a temporary situation, so I have made no such requests, and I believe it will be restored one day. MR. DI FAZIO: Would Your Honours just bear with me for a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've given evidence of having been arrested in Bosanski Samac, transferred to various places, to Batajnica, eventually to Pale, Sarajevo. Did you have any choice, any freedom of choice in your movements, in those movements that I've just described? Just answer yes or no, if you can.

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In April of 1992, before you were arrested, did you have any plans to leave and live your life away from Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had no such plans to leave Bosanski Samac. Even when all those events were taking place, I considered myself to be a man of integrity. I hadn't hurt anyone, I hadn't done anything wrong, so it never occurred to me to leave Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, I've pretty well come to the end of my examination-in-chief. I understand that you wanted me to address you briefly on another matter, and if I understood communications I received from registry, you wanted that to occur before this witness was released. Am I correct --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Regarding what? MR. DI FAZIO: The issue that was briefly touched upon yesterday, flying on from Judge Williams' question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Only if you feel it's necessary. Like I said, it's your indictment. If there are no proposals for amendment, fine, then there is no need. MR. DI FAZIO: I don't propose to -- no, I have no proposals to change the amendment or expand it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. Then that's fine. There is no need, then. MR. DI FAZIO: If the question troubles the Chamber and you want more submissions on it, I'm willing to do so, otherwise I'm happy to leave the matter as it stands.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. That's fine. We'll see how the evidence develops. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you. Well, in that case, can I indicate that I have no further questions of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Cross-examination. Who will start and who will follow? I just want to know the order, the sequence from the Defence counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, as Defence counsel for Mr. Zaric, I will be the one to begin with the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. And after yourself, who will follow, if any?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, on behalf of the Defence counsel for Mr. Miroslav Tadic, we will be the next after my colleague Mr. Pisarevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you. That's all, only two. Yes, you can start, Mr. Pisarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, all members of the Defence team will have a cross.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Good morning, Your Honours. I'm sorry. I just -- we thought that you wanted just the first two, but we are also going to cross-examine the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: You will decide who will begin between the two of you later.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Pisarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Only two from the rear bench and from the front bench, Mr. Zecevic and me finally.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Okay, that's fine, thank you. Yes, Mr. Pisarevic. You may start.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Cross-examined by Mr. Pisarevic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Izetbegovic. I think there is no need for me to introduce myself as we come from the same country, but I do wish to tell you that I am acting here as Defence counsel for Mr. Simo Zaric, and I wish to tell you in my own name and on behalf of Mr. Zaric that we sincerely regret everything that you have gone through in the course of those most unfortunate events in Bosnia-Herzegovina and we hope that it hasn't had grave consequences upon you. Mr. Izetbegovic, in your statement, you gave a short curriculum vitae and you mentioned your membership in the communist party, and later of the SDA, that is, the Party of Democratic Action of Bosnia-Herzegovina. You said that you were the founder of the municipal board of the SDA in Samac, so I would now like to ask you for us to look back to that period immediately prior to the formation of the SDA party in Samac. Would it be right to say that the Party of Democratic Action was the first national party formed in the territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina and also in the municipality of Bosanski Samac? Could you please answer yes or no.

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to say that I am not here on behalf of Bosnia-Herzegovina. I am only here on behalf of my survival in Bosanski Samac. I cannot speak on behalf of the state. I have no such authority. I can't say when the party was formed. I know that the branch of the party was the last to be formed in Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Izetbegovic, if you know, tell us; if you don't know, say you don't know. And if you don't, we won't continue along that line of questioning.

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In that case, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we agree that throughout that time, you were within the political leadership of the party, first as the president and then as the vice-president of the municipal board of the SDA for Bosanski Samac municipality?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As a person belonging to the top party leadership, were you consulted, informed, and involved in decision-making and the implementation of those decisions?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whatever we did, we did as a team, and there was never a decision taken by an individual, nor was it taken nor implemented on that basis.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we agree that the main purpose of the SDA was a struggle for the national interests of the Muslims in Bosnia-Herzegovina and the toppling of the communist authority?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We cannot.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we agree, then, that the Party of Democratic Action was a national party of the Muslim people?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't hear you quite. There was an interruption in the interpretation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we agree that the Party of Democratic Action was a national party of the Muslim people?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All three parties were national parties. There's no escaping that. What is important is what they actually did in the course of their development.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Izetbegovic, a moment ago I just asked you to answer yes or no. The Party of Democratic Action, was it also a religious party?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Surely religion is the private affair of each individual, and there was never particular emphasis in the party, nor were members obliged to be believers. In the civilised world, one is just asked whether you're a believer or not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you please answer this question: Are you familiar with the idea of certain elements in the Party of Democratic Action that by Islamisation of the area which they considered to be Muslim, to first create the first Muslim state in the Balkans since the collapse of the Ottoman Empire?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Never. Not even subconsciously would it occur to me to create a religious Islamic state, nor will that ever be achieved in the areas in which I live. That is why the party will always advocate -- will always struggle against that. That is a purely political party, and if it is to somebody's benefit to proclaim somebody guilty and then to look for sources of that guilt, that's another matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: May I remind the witness that just to answer the questions as they are put to you. The Trial Chamber is aware that you have other ideologies and your feelings are quite high during cross-examination, but please remember that counsel is asking the questions on behalf of the Trial Chamber, it is part of the proceedings; so please answer the questions, just answer them, and do not feel agitated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware or familiar with senior officials in the SDA of Bosnia-Herzegovina such as Omer Behmen, Hasan Cengic, Salim Sabic, and others?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know them well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that it was precisely Omer Behmen, Hasan Cengic, Salim Sabic, and others, insisted and worked towards a religious character for the Party of Democratic Action?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I do not know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: May we agree that in Bosnia-Herzegovina, areas did exist which the Muslims considered to be their own, that there were other areas which the Serbs considered belonged to them, and that areas existed which the Croats believed to be theirs historically?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If they did exist, then that was from time immemorial, not from yesterday. I did not have knowledge of these areas..

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In view of the fact that you were the president of the party in Samac, did you take part in the organisation and implementation of the first multiparty elections in 1990, in the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did, on the territory of my own municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. That's what I was asking you about. May we also agree that before the elections there existed an agreement between the national parties on the non-attack in the election campaign and the overthrow of the government hitherto?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you repeat that question? I'm not sure I understood it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. May we agree that before the elections an agreement had been reached amongst the national parties, that is to say, the SDA, the SDS, and the HDZ, that they had agreed not to attack in the election campaign in the common goal of overthrowing the government?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a certain amount of party tolerance, but there was never any question of an overthrow of government. That's how I understood it, at least.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there an agreement or not, no agreement of any such kind?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no agreement of any such kind.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that after the elections and the victory of the national parties at the elections in 1990, that the formation of organs of government and authority was formed on the principle of 5/4/3 in Bosnia-Herzegovina, and that meant five Muslims, four Serbs, and three Croats, along the lines of those ratios?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where do you mean? At what level?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm asking you about the level of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I am well aware of that, but I did not make any decisions along those lines. It was not up to me to decide.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the municipality of Samac, in view of the electoral results, was power divided exclusively between the Croatian Democratic Community, the Serb Democratic Party, and the Party of Democratic Action?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was divided up to the satisfaction of all three parties compared to the election results.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: May we agree that you, yourself, in that distribution, as a candidate, as the candidate of the SDA party, got the post of the vice-president of the executive board of the municipal board of Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we also agree that, according to this same principle, the representative of the Croatian Democratic Community, the HDZ, Mato Nujic , by ethnicity a Croat, was elected as the mayor, or president of the municipality?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And following on from that same principle, for the president of the Executive Council of the municipal assembly, as a member of the Serbian Democratic Party, Mirko Jovanovic was elected? May we agree there?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was elected. They nominated him and he was elected.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: May we also agree that that same principle of distribution of power was applied to the election of the leaders of the municipal administration?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I wouldn't put it that way. I don't think it was like that in the administration to the end. Some time elapsed. There weren't sufficient cadres, so some things did go through, other things were left unfinished.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you confirm that the following individuals performed functions which I'm going to enumerate now: Vinko Dragicevic, a Croat, was the chief of police; Zijada Kuckovic, a Muslim lady, was the president of the court, in Bosanski Samac, that is; Mirko Vasiljevic, a Serb, was the public prosecutor; Ivo Kobas, a Croat, commander of the staff of Territorial Defence; Milos Bogdanovic, a Serb, the head of the secretariat for national defence of the municipality of Bosanski Samac; Mato Madzarevic, a Croat, head of town planning. Are those the individuals who led the municipality administration in the Bosanski Samac municipality?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they are.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: May we then agree that in this division of power too, the principle was applied of what we called the national key, which was applied by the Communists in their day while they were in power as well?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was partially applied. The rest was left open -- the rest were left as they were, because we looked at the professionalism of the individuals who performed their posts and they were found to be sound.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct that as president of the municipal board of the SDA, you were replaced by Mr. Sulejman Tihic and that you yourself then became the vice-president of the municipal board of the SDA for the Samac municipality?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: May we also agree with the fact that you were still an active and influential member of the SDA party in the Samac municipality?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I wasn't involved in decision making, but I did stay in the party and work for it, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware of the fact that in the summer of 1991, a meeting was held of the main board of the Democratic Action Party at Igman?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which year did you say? Can you give me the date again?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. In 1991.

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the summer of 1991, you say. I attended those meetings on three occasions, so I'm not sure which one you mean.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I said the meeting at Igman.

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did have a meeting, one dealing with the electoral results, the second meeting was with respect to preparations for a population census, but that was in 1991. And the third meeting, the electoral results. We had no other meetings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember that you once attended a meeting of the main board which was held on the mountain called Igman, near Sarajevo, Mount Igman?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I have just enumerated the three meetings. I don't know the one you are talking about.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Do you know, furthermore, that at that particular meeting, a decision was reached about arming members of the SDA and Muslim people and their military and party organisation?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A decision of that kind was never reached, nor was it ever discussed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Are you aware of the fact that the municipal board of the SDA for Samac elaborated a mobilisation plan for members of the Muslim military units?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That plan was devised by someone at their own initiative.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What I was asking you was whether the municipal board of the SDA party, the Party of Democratic Action of Bosanski Samac compiled a mobilisation plan for the members of Muslim military units.

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was not a Muslim military unit; it was a unit to protect one's own safety.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware, Mr. Izetbegovic, that that military plan of that kind, a mobilisation plan, was compiled?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and that same plan was handed over to the municipal board with all the members and it was placed under the control of the authorities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please answer the questions that I am asking you. Was it compiled or was it not compiled?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't answer that question, put that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I should like to ask the Trial Chamber, faced with a situation of this kind, to explain to the witness that we would like an answer whether a mobilisation plan was compiled or not. Could he give a yes or no answer, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. I'm waiting for the interpretation. And if you don't know, say you don't know. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, before the witness says anything, just reading the transcript, it seems that he has answered the question. "Are you aware, Mr. Izetbegovic, that a military plan of that kind, a mobilisation, was compiled?" "Yes, and that same plan was handed over to the municipal board and ... placed under the control of the authorities." And then the next question is: Well, answer the question. But he has, as far as I can see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I see that. Following the transcript, yes. MR. DI FAZIO: It's a bit hard to know what he -- Mr. Pisarevic can expand on that answer, of course, but he has answered the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Agreed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I'm afraid I can't follow the transcript at the same time, so I apologise for insisting on that point. But I was prompted because Mr. Izetbegovic said, "I can't state an opinion on that. I can't answer that question." That was the last thing he said before I went ahead with my question again. But anyway, very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you agree that the municipal board of the SDA of Samac, Bosanski Samac, formed its Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did have a Crisis Staff, like all the other parties.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: May we agree that at the head of that Crisis Staff was Mr. Sulejman Tihic, the president of the municipal board of the SDA party of Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the hierarchy, that was quite normal, him and Alija Fitozovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: May we agree that you too were a member of that Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You formed a party and military formation made up of members of the SDA and Muslims from Bosanski Samac, did you not? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It never said that it was a party military formation anywhere.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you form an armed military formation?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not what it says either.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the commander of that particular formation Alija Fitozovic, a reserve Major of the Yugoslav People's Army from Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It wasn't a command; it was a unit which had a structure of power and authority and data and names. Nothing was confidential, actually. There was nothing secret about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That unit of yours, Mr. Izetbegovic, did it have a command?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, when the people had arms, it was probably normal to introduce some sort of order so that that should not be abused, but what they were doing was providing security for various premises, because there was no police force or militia, as we used to call it in town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Izetbegovic, would you refrain from elaborating and answer my questions. It will facilitate the work of one and all in these proceedings if you would be so kind as to do so. Were you yourself a member of that command which numbered five members?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A member of the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Izetbegovic, we have clarified the question of the Crisis Staff. What I'm asking you now is to tell me whether you were a member of the command of the armed unit which was formed and organised by the municipal board of the SDA of Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not aware of having been in that post. It was a list which was entitled "Crisis Staff." I don't know anything further than that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you happen to know the fact that a plan of attack existed, a plan of attack on Bosanski Samac, in collaboration with the HDZ?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: May we agree that on the municipality of Bosanski Samac, a Croatian Defence Council had been formed. The commander was reserve Captain Marko Bozanovic, by ethnicity a Croat?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I am not aware of that. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Microphone. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, may I just interrupt the cross-examination there. The question was asked by Mr. Pisarevic: "Do you happen to know the fact that a plan of attack existed, a plan of attack on Bosanski Samac, in collaboration with the HDZ?" Answer: "No, I'm not aware of that." Now, if Mr. Pisarevic is putting to the witness that there was in fact such a plan, then I submit that all of the circumstances of that alleged plan of attack should be put to the witness so that he can fully answer. And secondly, it should also be put so that the Tribunal -- the Chamber, rather, understands what is being put to the witness. Plan of attack with whom? Now, I think that what Mr. Pisarevic Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. is saying is that there was a plan of attack between the SDA and the HDZ. If so, then that should be clearly put, because at the moment it's not clear who was collaborating with the HDZ, who was being supposed or alleged to have collaborated with the HDZ, and I think that should be clarified.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I'm sure counsel has understood the point the Prosecution is making and will take that into account when cross-examining the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, of course, Your Honour. Thank you. However, there is an error in the transcript. I did not say with the HDZ. I said with the Croatian Defence Council.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Maybe you can repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The question was as follows: May we agree that a plan of attack existed on Bosanski Samac in collaboration with the HVO or Croatian Defence Council of the Bosanski Samac municipality?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you repeat that question once again?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we agree that a plan of attack existed on Bosanski Samac which was made up, which was devised by the command of the armed unit of the SDA with the Croatian Defence Council of Bosanski Samac municipality?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about a plan of that kind. Who would they attack? Themselves?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you do not know, did you perhaps happen to hear about the existence of such a plan?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me repeat the question because you didn't give me an answer. Do you agree that on the Bosanski Samac municipality, the HVO, Croatian Defence Council, had been formed and that the commander was reserve Captain Marko Bozanovic, by ethnicity a Croat?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have absolutely no idea what they did in their section.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. May we agree that the most responsible for performing all these preparations in the organisation of the municipal board of the Democratic Action Party was Mr. Sulejman Tihic, as party president?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We made decisions collectively. One person, one member, cannot be held responsible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We're not talking about responsibility, but we're talking about who the most responsible person was.

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's what I answered a moment ago; by hierarchy, it was the president.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: May we agree that you, Mr. Izetbegovic, and Alija Fitozovic, worked most to illegally arm the Party of Democratic Action and Muslims in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Izetbegovic, Mr. Tihic, in his recollections on page 12, states that you and Alija Fitozovic were most active in illegally arming the SDA and Muslims in Bosanski Samac. Is that assertion correct or not?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it is not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: May we agree that a significant role in the illegal arming of the Democratic Action Party and the Muslim people were held by Atif Rakic [as interpreted], Salkic Ibrahim, Dedo Halilovic, Aziz Hecimovic, Osman Mesic, Pasaga Tihic , Esad Hadzimujagic and Jasenica Fuad?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we can't agree with that. Each person brought their own weapons individually. Nothing was done in an organised fashion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me, please -- or rather, answer my question: Where is Slavonski Brod located, or rather, is Slavonski Brod to be found in the Republic of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you confirm the fact that you and Alija Fitozovic, on the 10th of January, 1992, from Mr. Meter and Mr. Piplovic, who were officers of the Croatian army in Slavonski Brod, which is located in the Republic of Croatia, received and brought into Bosanski Samac 100 kilogrammes of military explosives?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I only heard about that, but I didn't bring it or go to fetch it, and this is the first time that I'm hearing about Mr. Meter being an officer, and Mr. Piplovic as well. The first man was the mayor, and the other one was a politician. I know them as political figures both.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: However, I must tell you that Mr. Tihic, in his recollections on page 12, line 25, says the following: "Nevertheless, concrete business was done by Izet and Alija mostly."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Counsel, to interrupt you. Which -- what are you referring to? Is it the evidence in court of Mr. Tihic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. These are Mr. Tihic's recollections, which I'm sure at a certain stage of the proceedings will be evidence before this Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Was it the memoirs? MR. DI FAZIO: It's what I tried to introduce, and unless I'm wrong, there was an objection from Mr. Pisarevic, so ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: And they were not accepted in evidence. MR. DI FAZIO: No. You ruled against my being permitted to introduce them in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. So they are not part of the evidence, so you can't cross-examine the witness on them.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the first time that I've heard about those memoirs. It's something that I have not -- did not know about until hearing it now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: But how come you are referring to them? Because you see, when a document has not been admitted into evidence, you cannot introduce its contents by way of cross-examination, because they are not part of the evidence on record.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand, Your Honour, and I won't refer to the document again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: However, are you aware of the fact that - or perhaps you heard about it - that 100 kilogrammes of explosives were brought in from Slavonski Brod? Did you hear about that?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I only heard about it, but I can't discuss it further than that, and I am not claiming that it's true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Izetbegovic, did you ever go to Slavonski Brod?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did officially, as vice-president of the party. No, not -- of the Executive Council of the municipality, because of the blockade of the bridge and the question of traffic. There were five-kilometre-long columns of traffic and Bosanski Samac couldn't stand it any longer because of the blockade, and that was the only reason why I went there, because of the bridge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can you -- yes. Before the next question, can you just clarify again in what status you went to this place, because the answer is not clear.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I went there in the capacity of vice-president of the Executive Council of the municipal assembly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us: Who did you hear from about this explosive?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't tell you that. You know best how gossip gets around in our towns, so I can't name anyone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think that nevertheless, in this Trial Chamber, you should put aside gossip, and I think that this Trial Chamber has the right and duty to hear more precisely, so will you please give me an answer, or I will have to appeal to Their Honours for an answer from you. MR. DI FAZIO: Well, that's unfair, isn't it, if Your Honours please. He says -- the question, a perfectly proper question from Mr. Pisarevic: "From whom did you hear about this explosive?" The witness says, "I can't tell you." And then Mr. Pisarevic says, "Well, I have to appeal to the Trial Chamber for an answer." Now, if he can't tell us, he can't tell us, and that's the end of the matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No. If he knows the person who told him, he should, because he hasn't given reasons why he can't tell us the person who told him. MR. DI FAZIO: I see. Perhaps I've -- maybe I've misunderstood. If the witness is saying, "I can't tell you that" because he doesn't know, then surely that's the end of the matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Then he must say so. MR. DI FAZIO: If he's saying, "I can't tell you that" because he needs to protect an identity or something else, some other reason, that's another matter altogether. I'm not trying to stop him from that. Just on that, if there are reasons for -- if the reason is because he wants to protect someone, I'd ask that the Chamber give consideration to perhaps closing the Court during that evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Because he has to tell us his reasons first. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: And then we can go into private session and then we can have the name or he can write the name on a piece of paper - we've done that before - and then it would be under seal. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Madam President. That was exactly my idea, to go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right, then. Please sit down.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Madam President, but in addition, it's a matter of procedure. It's a matter of principle of law. In this particular case, Mr. Izetbegovic said that he knows who is in question, the person in question, but due to the small area, local atmosphere and gossips, he is not going to tell us here. But please advise the witness here that he is here before the Court of law and you are conducting the proceedings and then you have all kind of measures to go into private session or to, you know ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: But he knows, the fact is that he knows who the person is, so he answered that question. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: We explained that, I think, briefly. We didn't want it to go on and on and waste time. So the witness has understood what the Chamber has said in view of what the Prosecution raised. So if the witness knows the name and for reasons of security or whatever, he better tell us why he can't tell us the name of the person who informed him.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I heard when they asked me whether it was true, and I said I don't know. And the person who asked me didn't know either whether it was true. So it's a small place. There are all kinds of rumours going around. And that is my answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No. Now you are saying the person who told you also did not know whether it was true. That's not the point. We just want the name of the person who told you, rumour or fact. You've already explained that he said he didn't know whether it was true. So we just want the name, unless you have reasons to protect his name, in which case we shall resort to the measures that we have already spelled out.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think I have nothing more to say. I simply don't know. And I beg to be spared. After all, I am a witness here, I'm not an accused. Could I be spared questions which are not the subject of these proceedings? There are many other witnesses who will know more, and that particular person, I assume, will probably come here and be able to tell you more. I'm telling you what I know and as much as I know. If that is satisfactory for the Defence and for Your Honours and for the Prosecution, I can't say more than that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, Mr. -- MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I just wanted to get the interpretation concluded. MR. DI FAZIO: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, you wanted to say what? MR. DI FAZIO: Unless I'm wrong, I think there's just -- what's happening here is just a misunderstanding, unless I'm wrong. He has said, "I simply don't know." Now, I assumed that he's saying there, "I simply don't know the name."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, Mr. di Fazio. We've been through that. Okay. Let me ask him: Do you know the name of the person who told you about explosives?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm sorry. It is my understanding that this is really not acceptable. My learned colleague from the Prosecutor side is coaching the witness in a certain sense. That is one thing. The other thing is the witness clearly stated that this person who has told him will be a witness over here and you can ask him. That's in the transcript. So he knows who is the person, he knows that he's going probably to be a witness over here. He just doesn't want to give us his name. That's the point. And I mean -- and the Honourable Trial Chamber asked him to reveal the name of that particular person, and if the witness doesn't want to do that in the public session, let's go into the private session and then he can tell us. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, with your permission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All the questions I have put to the witness were because he hasn't given any serious reason why he should not tell the Trial Chamber that name.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Let me deal with it this way. Let's not go on and on. Mr. Izetbegovic -- I'm sorry, I can't pronounce the name at all. Witness, do you have any misgivings about giving the Trial Chamber the name of this person? If you do, we can go into private session, in which case that name will not be revealed to members of the public but it will be revealed to the people in court, that's the Trial Chamber, the counsel, and the accused persons.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't think I have hidden or concealed anything so far. Whatever I know, I have said. I realise I have to tell the truth. I have mentioned many names. I wasn't afraid. I am not afraid about this one. Simply, if something is being said in town, I can't tell you who told me. It is not reliable, because I myself didn't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. You know that this type of conduct will go to the credibility of your evidence. It will affect how the Trial Chamber, you know, assesses the quality of your evidence, because you have said maybe this person will be called as a witness or did you imply that you have no idea? Because the impressions we get is that you do know this person. I'll ask you again: Do you know that person or not? It's up to you whichever answer you give. I've told you the consequences.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said that probably that person would come here. I was thinking of Alija Fitozovic, who is mentioned in that connection. If he did that, and I'm saying if, he will probably give all the answers. I cannot provide answers, because I was not a participant of everything. And that was the person I had in mind. If you have to squeeze this out of me, if that is so important to the Defence or to the Court, I don't understand why that should be so important. I think there are many more important things.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No. It is for the Trial Chamber to decide what is important, and that's why we stop some questions sometimes, if you have observed that. Counsel, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us clear up some things, then.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could counsel speak into the microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Counsel, please speak into the microphone because the interpreters can't get what you're saying.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The question that was put to you was: From whom did you hear that Alija Fitozovic had obtained the explosives, or did Alija Fitozovic tell you about it, the person you just mentioned?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I appeal to you once again to spare me this kind of provocation. I have told you everything I knew about the explosives and the part I played in that. I know nothing more than that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Izetbegovic, I have no intention to aggravate the situation in any way, but we have to clear things up. My question was: Who told you about the explosives?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've given you my answer. I have nothing more to say about explosives.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that the story was that it was Alija Fitozovic. That's not the same.

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Rumour is rumour. I cannot tell you. Mr. Pisarevic, Mr. Attorney, I don't know the name of an individual. If that means anything to you, take it that I said it, but I don't know and I don't have a name.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Counsel, can we proceed? Can you go to other questions? We've heard enough of this, and I think the answer is in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Izetbegovic, do you know a person by the name of Senahid Memic, from Hrasnica in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you confirm the fact that Mr. Memic asked you and Mr. Tihic to assist him when his truck, packed full with illegal weapons that he was driving from Croatia to Bosnia-Herzegovina, sought assistance?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No one asked for my assistance then, because I was in Sarajevo at the time, attending a session.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know the fact that he asked Mr. Tihic for that assistance?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that near the mosque in Bosanski Samac, the weapons were reloaded into a truck of the veterinary station of Bosanski Samac, which the driver of which was Smail Smailovic from Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that either.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Mr. Pisarevic, just one question. What was the date when all of this was happening, the transfer of the weapons and so on? Because I find it may be -- it would be of assistance to the Tribunal and also to the witness when being asked these types of questions and where he was at the time, to know exactly what we're talking about in terms of the date. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I understand, Your Honour, your advice.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Izetbegovic, the session, the meeting you mentioned that you attended on that day, when did it take place, if you can tell us? Tell us just the month and year, you don't have to give us the day.

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember the date, but I know that that was the day that the bridge was blown up. I was in Sarajevo when I heard about it being blown up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we agree, then, that this was the 23rd of March, 1992?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If that is when that happened, then that is the date. I'm not very good with dates.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, yes, the 23rd. Could you please explain your answer when you said -- when I asked you about the breakdown of the truck, you said, "I was that day in Sarajevo attending a meeting." Had you heard about this incident?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let's try and come to some agreement. Whatever I say in my answer, I had heard about. I heard about this truck and everything after I left the camp. I learnt about many things which I hadn't known before. So I didn't know that then. I was attending a meeting in Sarajevo regarding the budget of the municipality. I didn't know what was happening in Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Izetbegovic, please, whatever you heard afterwards or what you don't know, just please tell us that you don't know, so I won't ask you anything further about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: In fairness to the witness, you, Counsel, should be stating the dates. At what stage did you know, when did you hear about this? If you want the witness to be answering the questions the way you've just explained. Because it's not fair when you're not particular with dates yourself.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, in view of the fact that these were illegal matters, we are not in possession of data indicating the exact date, time, hour, so I cannot ask Mr. Izetbegovic whether this happened on such-and-such a day at such-and-such a time, because all this was being done illegally. I have some information about this, but I cannot give the exact hour or day or month. I can give the month or year, but I really -- it is very difficult for us to gain possession of such data.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Even the participants in those events.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: It's a long time, I appreciate that, and as you say, these were illegal activities at that time in that locality. It's not the exact date. At least the month, the year, or was it the first half of this year or the second half or the first quarter, something like that at least, so that the witness is properly guided.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Izetbegovic, did you have any knowledge, as a member of the Crisis Staff and as a member of the command, that on that occasion when the weapons were being reloaded, Mr. Memic, from the SDA of Bosanski Samac, gave 20 automatic rifles and 2.000 rounds in March 1992?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As a member of the Crisis Staff, you can address me, but not as a member of the command. My answer is: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know of the fact that Senahid Memic and Bakir Alispahic, in a white Golf, licence place SA 335-820 arrived in this car and handed over to the president of the SDA of Bosanski Samac in January 1992, 30 automatic rifles M-56?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To which president? There were two.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The president of the municipal board of the SDA of Samac. Who was president at the time?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Tihic, I think. When your question is complete, I'll give you an answer. When you have a complete question, I'll give you an answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I need clarification here. We've got the answer. Mr. Tihic was the president at this time. Is the answer also yes to the fact that this was -- whatever was being handed over, the arms were being handed over to the president? Can we have clarification from the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do not know the details, but I heard about it from Alija Fitozovic. So there's no need to go any further than that. At the time I was not president, Mr. Attorney. I think you've got your answer after all.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Izetbegovic, I didn't say that you were president. I don't know what the interpretation is that you are getting. I never said that you were the president, at the time, of the SDA.

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm getting a good interpretation, but I asked you to tell me who was the president.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Counsel and Witness, you are not in conversation. We are in a trial. Please stick to the rules of procedure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: Mr. Pisarevic, when you do ask questions, I know that you have instructions and you have a brief. We don't have your instructions and we don't have your brief, so please lay the foundation of your questions first so that we can follow them. Now, Memic, one would expect you to ask him: Do you know a person by the name of so-and-so, and then you move from there, and please ask one question at a time. I notice that in your questions you have a number of them, and sometimes again we don't know to which question he is giving an answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Thank you for your guidance, Your Honour. I shall do my best to break down my questions, but I thought this would be more expeditious.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware of the fact, as a member of the Crisis Staff, that on the 15th of April, 1992, Jasenica Fuad and Salkic Ibrahim brought by car 50 automatic rifles, two mortars, several hand-held rocket launchers and some ammunition?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do know. I don't know the composition, but all that was immediately placed at the disposal of the Territorial Defence, accompanied by all the necessary documents. Nothing was done illegally.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you confirm the fact that these weapons were brought in from Slavonski Brod, which is situated in the Republic of Croatia, and that it was obtained from the Croatian army?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't confirm that fact, because I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You don't know one of them or you don't know any of those facts?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which three?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That it was brought from Slavonski Brod. Can you confirm that fact?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Counsel, you didn't take the direction from Judge Singh of loading your own questions and you're caught up by your own problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: Mr. Izetbegovic, can I ask you one question. You said that you were a member of the Crisis Staff. I take it that it's the Crisis Staff of the SDA. What was the crisis in response to which the Crisis Staff was formed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Crisis Staff existed. We self-organised ourselves because we realised we had been left alone. Everyone had his own group. We just organised ourselves to protect our own property, and this staff was also under the control of the legal authorities and SUP. They guarded and controlled our buildings and our facilities, because no one was there to protect us and there were long lines of columns, foreigners, outsiders, and we wanted to protect ourselves from unknown persons because businesses were being blown up and all kinds of other things, and we were protecting our own houses and our own businesses, and this staff had no other intention and no other programme, and this was made public daily. The daily people on duty were listed, so that all this was done in coordination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we take our break and we'll resume our proceedings at 11.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Pisarevic is to continue. Yes, Prosecution. MR. DI FAZIO: Perhaps before Mr. Pisarevic starts, there's just a brief evidential matter that I want to raise. It does affect Mr. Pisarevic's cross-examination, but indeed it's a general matter that I raise. In the cross-examinations thus far, and in this particular cross-examination, I have noticed very little in the way of putting of one's case to the witnesses, very little. And indeed under Rule 90(G) -- sorry, (H), 90(H)(2), that topic is addressed. It says: "In the cross-examination of a witness who is able to give evidence relevant to the case for the cross-examining party, counsel shall put to that witness the nature of the case of the party for whom that counsel appears which is in contradiction of the evidence given by the witness," similar to what I'm familiar with in my jurisdiction known as the rule in Brown and Dunne and it's a rule of fairness, so that the witness is able to comment on what Defence counsel may later say to the Chamber. Now, as I say, it's not a matter of concern for the Prosecution and it's not a matter for us to direct Defence counsel on how they conduct their cross-examinations, but as far as Defence counsel are concerned, I think they should be aware that if they don't do that, then that will certainly be a matter of comment from the Prosecution at the end of the case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you very much for pointing it out, and the Trial Chamber has been observing this and in fact has discussed this very matter. The three of us did discuss this as a matter to be observed, and I'm sure that the Defence counsels have read these Rules and do know that the Rules are in force and will apply to these proceedings. We come from different legal systems, as you know, and the art of cross-examination may not be familiar to all the people involved in these proceedings before the Tribunal, so usually there is need for guidance, but the Trial Chamber does expect that the Defence counsel, as well as the Prosecution counsel, do read these Rules and they do understand them and they know that they apply. So one can only hope that the Rules will be complied with and the cross-examination will try to elicit the Defence case, if any, and leave it at that. Thank you. Mr. Pisarevic, please continue your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, may we just have a few moments to confer, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: Mr. Izetbegovic, I just want to have one more follow-up question from the Crisis Staff that the SDA have. Was this Crisis Staff formed in response to some other party having a Crisis Staff? Was there another set of Crisis Staff belonging to other parties at about that time, in 1991, December or so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All parties had Crisis Staffs, and that's what we did, we sat down to set up a Crisis Staff. But its sole purpose was self-protection and self-organisation for the preservation and protection of property, nothing else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Perhaps I could just follow up on my colleague Judge Singh's question. Which Crisis Staff was formed first? Was it that of your party or was it the other parties? So was yours in response, was yours set up first, set up second, set up third?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was set up third.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Counsel, please proceed and please stand nearer the microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Yes, I will. I have understood the point made by the Prosecution and the guidance given by the Trial Chamber. I nonetheless consider that, according to Rule 90(H)(1), (A)(1) or (H)(1), during the examination-in-chief, when matters affecting the credibility of the witness are in question, that one may introduce evidence which have been disclosed previously, but if there are certain -- if there is a lack of clarity, I shall try my best to do away with that. First and foremost, I should like now to introduce a piece of evidence. It is a document which the municipal Crisis Staff, with its members, has, and it was disclosed to the Prosecution and copies were prepared for all participants in the trial. I should like to request that that document be shown to the witness and to be given a number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Okay. I take it that it will be shown to the witness in sequence, as they appear in the file, or is it the intention of counsel to have one collective number and then we can have /1, /2, whatever? How is the counsel going to use the documents?

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, there could be one collective number and then perhaps /1, /2, /3, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: And all of them, I can see, do have Serbo-Croat and English translation. Okay. Yes. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. The Prosecution have received these documents? MR. DI FAZIO: I believe we have, but I'm not sure that I know which particular documents are being spoken about at this stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Probably the whole file. MR. DI FAZIO: I've got a file here that my --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: How many documents do you have in there? MR. DI FAZIO: Five.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, five. So they will be introduced in that order. And you've looked at them, I suppose, because I'm trying to ask what is your position. MR. DI FAZIO: They've been disclosed and they're properly translated, so I've got no objection at this stage to their going in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can we have the number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Number for the exhibits will be D2/4, continuing to D3/4, D4/4, and D5/4, and D6/4.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: And the Serbo-Croat? Because we've been using "ter" at the end of the numbering for the Serbo-Croat.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: For the Serbo-Croat, it will be D2/4 ter, D3/4 ter, D4/4 ter, D5/4 ter, and D6/4 ter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, the only thing, as I read the transcript, I have no problem with the documents going in, but which one is which?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Oh, I see. I did say in the sequence as presented. So maybe I'll ask the registry assistant -- or maybe I'll ask the Defence counsel how he understands the numbering and then he will take us through which is D2/4. You could deal with that. Yes, let the registry assistant deal with that, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The first document is D2, the municipal Crisis Staff, number 2, the municipal Crisis Staff. The next document is annex number 3, the municipal Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Excuse me. Can we have the registry assistant read the numbers for us all, so that we follow the numbers as recorded by the registry assistant. I'm sorry. It does not mean that is the sequence of importance, no, and you can actually start with any one of them, but we just want to be clear as to which document is which number for the time being, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document D2/4 will be the municipality Crisis Staff document annex number 2. Document D2/4 [sic] municipality military document annex number 3. Document D4/4 will be a receipt. Document D5/4 is a certificate received by Mr. Izetbegovic. Document D6/4 is a receipt number 1342, dated, I think, the 2nd of March, 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: And then the Serbo-Croat parts follow the same numbering with a "ter" at the end.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: With a "ter." That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honours. There is just one mistake in the transcript and I believe the registrar made it, actually. It says here two documents D2/4. This is 42nd page, 9 and 10, rows 9 and 10. It says document D2/4 will be the municipality Crisis Staff document, annex number two. D2/4, municipality military document. This should be D3, if I correctly understood.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Which one should be D3?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: The document, the second document which is named "municipality military headquarters."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: According to your understanding should be?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: D3/4, and in the transcript it says D2/4 twice. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Let her repeat, correct it again.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: If I may add, Your Honour. This is the municipality document, the military headquarters, with annex number 3 on the right upper corner. That's D3/4 for the English, and D3/4 ter for the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes. Counsel can go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I should like to ask the usher's assistance to show the witness document D2/4, municipality Crisis Staff, annex number 2, copy number 2.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I should now like to ask the witness to read the document, to have a look at it. Have you acquainted yourself with the contents of the document, Mr. Izetbegovic?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know this document? Have you seen it before?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never saw it before coming to The Hague. I learnt of it when I came to The Hague.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that this is the municipality Crisis Staff of the SDA?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is the Crisis Staff. I don't know why municipal, municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you agree with me that you - that is to say, not you personally but the SDA party - gave it the name of the municipality Crisis Staff, that's how you named it?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if it says so, then that is what it was. And if it has a signature, but I can't see any signature. I'd like to be able to see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I should now like to ask you to read the name of the president of the municipality Crisis Staff. It says here Sulejman Tihic, but I don't see anybody's signatures here. Is your name on the list at all, and if so, where?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see that it is a name under "members."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me what the numbers on the document signify, 61459, 61204, and so on?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see that 61204 is my home telephone number.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I should like the witness to be shown document D3/4 next, please. It is annex number 3 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Counsel, to interrupt you, but before we leave this document, when the witness says, "I can see the number is my home telephone number," is it the number today or was it the number then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the next heading is "municipality military headquarters," and it says that the president is Fitozovic, Alija. Are you acquainted with this document?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you agree that your name is on the document?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see that it is on the document, but nobody asked me about anything like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know the individuals on the document? Do you know Fitozovic, Alija?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know all the people, but this is the first time that I'm seeing my name on a document of this kind. Nobody asked me or consulted me whether I wanted to be amongst them or not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
