utterances.text: But you were the vice-president of the party nonetheless. Was that customary in the SDA for such high-ranking functionaries to be put on lists without their knowledge and agreement?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it wasn't customary for anybody to be put on a list without their acquiescence; not only presidents, but anybody.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These telephone numbers, are they numbers dating back to 1992?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mine is. I don't know about the others.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the usher show the witness the next document, which is D4/4. It is a receipt dated the 10th of January, 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Pisarevic. I'd like to ask Mr. Izetbegovic a question, which is: Could you tell us what is the difference in principle between the municipality Crisis Staff, on the one hand, and the municipality military headquarters, on the other hand. Apart from the membership, but the difference in principle between the two groups. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All I can say is that the Crisis Staff existed within the party, but it was never titled the "municipality Crisis Staff." I don't know why that word "municipality" is there. Probably they might have been thinking about the municipality but it never had a municipality function on behalf -- to do anything on behalf of the whole municipality. It was only a Crisis Staff within the party. And this is the first time I'm seeing these other documents. I have never had access to them. I don't know about them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: So you don't know what the municipality military headquarters was or did?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was never called "military" either. I don't know who named it that way and with what right. It was just called the "Crisis Staff of the party." Somebody compiled this. How they compiled it, I don't know, but it was without my agreement. Actually, he didn't -- wasn't duty-bound to inform me of everything, because I wasn't a leading person of the party.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In connection with those two documents, I just have one more question. All the individuals on these lists, on these documents, are they members of the SDA?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I assume they are. I didn't have that registry. The secretariat had all the members listed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are the members of Muslim ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they are. I assume they are. It is their right to state their own ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us look at the next document, which is D4/4. It is a receipt, as I said, dated January 10th, 1992, confirming that Dzananovic Nerfid received 20 kilogrammes of explosives of the Vitezit type 20 and 12 M of slow-burning stick. Do you know Nerfid Dzananovic?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the right-hand corner, you will see it says Fitozovic Alija. Actually, it says Fitozovic, A. And underneath that, it says "Atif Rakic" [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are they members of the SDA party?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they are, but these aren't their signatures. The person who wrote this receipt, that is his signature.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us - if you can, do so - whose signature is to be found under where it says "delivered by"?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now I'd like to ask you to take a look at the next document, D5/4. This is a certificate, certifying the reception of 04, M160 and so on and so forth. Have you ever seen this certificate?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my testimony previously, I said that we had some weapons which we distributed with regular receipts and full control as to who had them and why they had them, and that is no secret, that we procured weapons. I also said that. So probably - I can't remember any more. I did have a pistol from the party - whether that is that, I don't know - which the party procured for its people, and I did sign that. That's no secret. I never used it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this your signature on the certificate?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is my signature, Mr. Pisarevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This ammunition mentioned here, could you tell us what it means, 04 and M160?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm afraid I don't know that either. It was a long time ago.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could that be pistol ammunition perhaps?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. It could be.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could it be ammunition for a Kalashnikov?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never had any such thing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you're claiming that you never had a Kalashnikov?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't remember having it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me remind you. Kalashnikov is an automatic rifle manufactured in Russia.

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do know what a Kalashnikov is, but I don't know that I had one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you please look at document D6/4. It is a receipt with the number 1342, dated the 2nd of March, 1992, in the name of Atic Ratif [as interpreted]. Do you know Atic Ratif [as interpreted]?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is Ratif Atic [as interpreted] from Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is Ratif Atic [as interpreted] a Muslim by ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You should ask him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is Mr. Atic [as interpreted], as far as you know, was he a member of the SDA?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you please look under entry number 1. It says "9-mm Luger long, 5.000 pieces." What is that?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then item number 2. It says 7.62 ammunition ZAG 2.520. Do you know what that is?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You yourself told what it is, but I don't know what it is in this document. I don't even know what that ammunition looks like.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: 7.20 -- 7.62 ammunition, and it says 2.520, and then "marking ammunition" 7.62, 1.260. Would you look at the stamp and tell us what it says.

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't read it. It is illegible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you be kind enough, Mr. Izetbegovic, to look at the original of that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the usher show the witness the original, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: What is the original? Yes, can counsel give it to the usher. And before you show it to the witness, can the Prosecutor see it, please.

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not an original. This is a photocopy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No. The one the witness has is a photocopy, but what is claimed to be the original is being looked at, examined by the Prosecution first. MR. DI FAZIO: This appears to be an original document. A carbon copy but -- [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Microphone. It appears to be what? MR. DI FAZIO: Sorry. This appears to be a carbon copy, but it is an original carbon copy, in other words, it hasn't got the Byro direct onto it, but it's obviously an original document, appears to be an original document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can the Trial Chamber please see it before it is shown to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: Mr. Pisarevic, do you have other carbon copies, originals of all the documents you have now given to the Court?

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I don't have them, sir, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: What we are looking at is a carbon copy. It has a stamp. And we will have it marked and we would like it also produced into evidence, because it is important to look at this as well, if this is what you call the original. Can we have it marked, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be --

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I quite agree, Your Honour, but I would like to say that I just asked Mr. Izetbegovic whether the stamp is the original. The stamp is the original over carbon. You see, the stamp cannot go through a carbon, so the stamp is original.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, but because it's important that we have sight of what you call the original, it's important that we have it in evidence as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, indeed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... and then it can be shown to the witness and then he can answer any questions.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The document will be marked D7/4 ter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. It's in Serbo-Croat. Yes. Okay. Thank you. Then it can be shown to the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Attorney, if you're asking me to read this, I will read it. It says: "Military post number, I don't know what, Slavonski Brod." That's all that I'm able to say regarding this document, because this is the first time I'm seeing this document. I don't know anything about it and I can't discuss it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you agree with me in saying that Slavonski Brod is in the republic of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is in Croatia. Where else?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could we agree, then, that Ratif Atic [as interpreted], as a member of your party, or rather, of the SDA, went to Croatia, and in the Republic of Croatia obtained ammunition and weapons?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say anything. Neither did I give any such instructions, nor was I consulted over such matters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Let me move on to another topic now, and please answer my question. Would you agree with me in saying that in the municipality of Samac, there was a hunters' organisation known as "Fazan," pheasant?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The exact name of the hunters' organisation is not known to me as I am not a hunter. I hear for the first time that it was called "Fazan," but there was such an organisation in existence for a long time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware of the fact that a large number of hunters were of Muslim ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were some, but I don't know how many and I can't tell you what the ratio was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we agree that a significant number of members of the hunters' association who were of Muslim ethnicity were also members of the Party of Democratic Action?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was absolutely their right, to join whichever party they wanted. What more is there to be said? There were certainly some who were not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that those hunters were also members of an armed unit which the SDA formed in Samac?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could I ask a distinction to be made? Let us leave the hunters alone. I don't know anything about that. In each ethnic group there were hunters, and they were normally in their parties. We had no cooperation with hunters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Just answer the question. Do not go ahead or, you know, explain anything if you think counsel's questions are leading to something else. Just answer the question as it is put to you. And Counsel, also remember to let the answer get completed before you start speaking because the interpretation is overlapping.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll do my best, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we agree that hunters were armed with hunting rifles and carbines?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. Hunters always had that, with a licence issued by the authorities. Now, who belonged to what, I don't know. They organised themselves. That was quite legal.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you agree with me in saying that a carbine is a hunting weapon with optical sights?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Don't ask me a lot about hunting weapons or trophy weapons. I don't know anything about these others either. I'm a layman about these things, and I'm sure there were carbines. Every well-off hunter had a carbine who could afford to buy one. Now, what ethnicity he was is something that I'm not interested in. Everyone had it, that is, whoever could afford it, and this was for game, used for large game.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you agree with me in saying that carbines with optical sights are in fact weapons known as "snipers"?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is very difficult, Mr. Attorney, to answer your questions, because one question contains ten others. I can see where you're heading. I'm asking you once again: Don't ask me anything about weapons. I simply will not answer those questions, because I don't know anything about weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just say you don't know.

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. That's all we need from you in the situation where you don't know the answer or you don't know what is being described and you are being asked to agree, you simply say you don't know.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, and I'm saying that I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you familiar with an organisation called the Patriotic League in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard about this after the camp and in the camp. I was neither a member nor do I know where it was, how it was, and things like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we then agree that you don't know?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What the tasks and objectives were of the Patriotic League, and that was the military organisation of the Muslims and arming them by illegal means.

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Izetbegovic, can you confirm that the SDA, the Party of Democratic Action, was in a coalition with the Croatian Democratic Community, the HDZ?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never saw any such document and I know that we were not in a coalition. We were not in a coalition with anyone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you, on behalf of the SDA party, hold and participate in certain meetings with representatives of the Croatian Democratic Community of Samac municipality?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We never did. There was an attempt, but I managed to break it up, and nothing happened, nothing came of it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you remember that a meeting of representatives of the Party of Democratic Action and of the Croatian Democratic Community was held in the Croatian village of Rudo on the 19th of March, 1992?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember there was one such meeting. That was the meeting I mentioned, and upon the initiative of certain individuals. It wasn't properly organised. I went to that meeting uninvited, uninvited, and I expressed my opinion and my position, which is to be found on the tape. I said everything I thought about the meeting on that tape. I didn't accept it, and nothing came of it, and there was never a joint Crisis Staff or anything like that formed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, excuse me. I believe there is some misunderstanding here in the transcript. Mr. Pisarevic asked about village Prud, and on the transcript we have Rudo. This is also a village in Bosnia, and this could possibly make some misunderstanding here, so just ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Can counsel clarify that, please, what he meant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: I wonder, Mr. Pisarevic, if I could just ask Mr. Izetbegovic: What is this tape that you mentioned from this meeting in the village of Prud?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The tape which was directed and produced by Mr. Zaric when I was interrogated in the MUP. I said what I had to say about that meeting and I uphold what I said then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I understand you mean the videotape that we saw yesterday. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can we have the correction regarding what your colleague mentioned in the transcript, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, indeed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it in the Croatian village of Prud?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Prud, Prud.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown, please, a map, P9, Exhibit P9, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please show on this map the location of the town of Samac and the location of the Croatian village of Prud.

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This should be the town of Samac, and Prud would be over here, on the other side of the Bosna River. I assume that is where it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can you leave your pointer there where you are saying Prud should be over here, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Izetbegovic, look a little more closely at the map, please. You can see number 99 on the map. That could help.

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where is that number? Oh, I see.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you see a word written there.

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, that's Prud. Yes. Yes, yes, that's it. I knew it was right next to the Bosna River. Yes, yes. This is the village of Prud and this is the inhabited area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: As it's shown on the exhibit. Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. For the record, may I say that the witness pointed on the map, Exhibit P9, the location of the town of Bosanski Samac and the location of the Croatian village of Prud.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could we agree that Mr. Sulejman Tihic attended that meeting together with you?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you agree that at the meeting there was also Alija Fitozovic, not Izetbegovic, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Be careful. You mustn’t make such mistakes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Alija Fitozovic?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Alija Fitozovic was there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And at that meeting were also present Filip Evic, a Croat, president of the municipal board of the HDZ of Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was, if that is what you're asking.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Mr. Mato Nujic also present at that meeting, a Croat, member of the HDZ and president of the Municipal Assembly of Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that he was there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you confirm that Mr. Mato Madzarevic was present at the meeting, a Croat and a member of the HDZ from Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you confirm that Mr. Slavko Matic was also present at the meeting, a Croat and a member of the HDZ from the Croatian village of Domaljica [phoen]?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Mr. Dragicevic, Vinko, present at the meeting, a Croat and chief of police of Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't notice him either.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Mr. Marko Bozanovic present at the meeting, a Croat and a member of the HDZ, a reserve military officer, that is, captain first-class?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think he was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Mr. Ivo Kobas present, a Croat and a commander of the territorial staff of the municipality of Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the meeting attended by Mr. Franjo Barukcic, a Croat from Bosanski Samac and a member of the HDZ?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Also I didn't see him. He is deceased. I don't know why he should be, he wasn't any ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At that meeting, did you make a decision to form a crisis -- a joint Crisis Staff which was headed by Filip Evic, a Croat and president of the municipal board of the HDZ for Samac?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Such a proposal was made at the meeting, and that was the reason why I went to see what the reason for the meeting was. I stood up resolutely immediately I realised where that was leading. I said it was out of the question, and I also said that the SDA party would not take part in such a meeting, and we walked out of it. Possibly afterwards they may have formed something, but without the SDA party.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you familiar with the fact that it was decided at that time that the commanders of the joint armed units should be Marko Bozanovic, a Croat, an officer in reserve of the Yugoslav People's Army with the rank of captain, and Mr. Alija Fitozovic, a Muslim and a member of the SDA, an officer in reserve of the Yugoslav People's Army with the rank of major?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As we walked out, I don't know what happened afterwards.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just one more question about that meeting. Was the meeting also attended by representatives of the Croatian army?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't notice anyone in uniform.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Braco, or rather, Stjepan Blazanovic, was he present at the meeting?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Personally, we never knew each other. I saw him for the first time. Yes, he was at that meeting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I shall now ask you a few questions about the general situation in Samac municipality, Mr. Izetbegovic, so will you tell me, please: Can we agree that the SDA was not satisfied with the public security station's activities and work in Bosanski Samac, that is, the work of the police?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know why it would have expressed its dissatisfaction when, at one point in time, the SDS withdrew its members and the HDZ withdrew its members - I said that in my earlier testimony - and the town was left without protection. Citizens were mobilised as reserve policemen so as to maintain some sort of continuity, because the police, or militia as it was called in those days, had been formed in the SDS, which had its base in Crkvina, and the HDZ had its own base in Domaljevac. So clearly, as there were few people available who could fill in the vacancies, filled them in, and those were the citizens, people who were willing to assist, who were willing to cooperate. These others didn't want to be in MUP. There were a few of them individually, but nothing more could be done by then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me now whether any diversions took place, whether there were any diversions, and whether any diversion was solved or sabotage was solved, or were the perpetrators of those sabotage incidents taken to prison?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't discuss that because, in the kind of work I did, I wouldn't have known. I don't know what the police did, whether the police solved situations of that kind or not, and how it did, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well, but do you agree that in the police force of Bosanski Samac the leading policemen were Vinko Dragicevic, a Croat, and Dragan Lukic, also a Croat?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Dragan stayed on from the previous make-up, but the other man was appointed by the HDZ.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But they're both Croats?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they are, both of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you agree with me that the police force was composed of the regular duty policemen and reserve police force?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, at the beginning that's how it was, because it was a big area which had to be covered, and there weren't enough men to do it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: May we agree with the fact that in the reserve composition of the police force in Bosanski Samac, the majority of those were Muslims that made up the reserve composition of the police force in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, what can you expect when nobody wants to go to the police station and be a member, when nobody wants to come from the Croatian part? You know that the Muslims were in town. The municipality of Samac does not have a single village that is Muslim, so it was quite normal that it was these people who were mobilised when no other side wanted to. They had to keep law and order in some way. The Muslims did not impose Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. themselves. They were called up and they responded to the call.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, yes. Do we agree that the majority of them were Muslims?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, following on from that logic, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we agree with the fact that the political forces filled in the -- put forward people for the police force and names for the police force?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. All sides, all parties put forward their own people, and then, once again, according to the electoral procedure and principle, the percentages were set, but it was the -- the parties were asked to put forward their own people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: May we agree, then, that the complement of the reserve police force was not done by the secretariat for national defence, as is the law?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The secretariat for national defence no longer existed either. That had disbanded as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it because of this uncertainty and insecurity and the general state of affairs as it was, that the SDA started to form party patrols which had their checkpoints during the night in the town of Samac itself?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely because of the prevailing situation, one in which there was no security any more. There was no safety for the citizens of the town. The Muslims saw to that. They had the right to self-organisation to protect themselves. That was the sole purpose, and none other.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: May we agree, then, that the situation in the municipality was one of general chaos and uncertainty and insecurity because the authorities were not functioning properly?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but quite certainly it was not the townsfolk of the town of Samac that caused the situation. This came with the overthrow of power and authority and all the rest of it. But they were able to keep law and order as far as they were able, and the different institutions functioning as far as they were able.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The patrols, your patrols, the SDA patrols, were they armed?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They weren't the classical type of patrol, as you seem to indicate. They were citizens that had been attached to the militia station, as it was called then. A list would be sent to the duty officer with all the names. Nothing was done illegally. Everything was above board. And they, together with the members of the regular police force, would tour the town and protect it, look for its security. Of course, some of them had weapons, some of them were armed, and that is no secret. Nobody is trying to say otherwise.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did those patrols have their own radio communication?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know, except what they had received from the police force, from the police station, the Motorola type. Some people got this so that they could call in and report from the locality they were at.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you happen to remember, or do you know that at the entrance points to the town of Bosanski Samac barricades had been set up at the end of March 1993 -- 1992, I'm sorry. 1992.

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am aware of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me, or will you agree with me when I say that those barricades were erected by the Democratic Action Party side?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't think we could say that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What, then, do you know? Who erected the barricades at the entrance to Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I assume somebody who needed them, but at this point, I don't know. I can't say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Izetbegovic, did you at the time, following orders from your president, Mr. Tihic, go to the organised Yugoslav People's Army in Brcko?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did go, and I went to say that the party does not stand behind that and that the party tried and did its best to do away with the barricades, and I went to state that, to say that we weren't behind those barricades, that they were individuals who had done what they had done. That's what happened. And I cannot say of those individuals that they were party members. And I didn't go alone. I was accompanied by the federal MUP inspector, who was also present. We went officially to set ourselves apart from that because we were not involved in it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you assert the fact that the barricades at the entrance to the town of Samac were erected by unruly members of the Democratic Action Party?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you for giving them such a mild qualification. It is true that each side, every side has unruly members, even families have unruly family members. I don't want to give a negative answer. Probably there were some unruly members who had these ideas in their heads, but there were many others too.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm sorry. We have a problem with the transcript. It's 62, page 62, under 17. It says "go to the organised Yugoslav People's Army in Brcko." It didn't say "organised." It said kazerne or something like that, military barracks. If this can be clarified, please. There is Yugoslav -- it says here in the --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could counsel --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... row 17, page 62, it says, "Go to the organised Yugoslav People's Army in Brcko," and the witness has said the garrison of the Yugoslav People's -- or the question was the garrison of Yugoslav People's Army in Brcko.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters kindly ask counsel to speak into the microphone, otherwise we find it very hard to hear him sometimes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pisarevic, do stand near the -- I keep thinking that maybe you should swap places with your co-counsel, I think, so that you are nearer the microphone. Yes. And can you clarify this with the witness, the military -- what was it? The organised -- whatever it was called. Can you clarify that with the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Izetbegovic, did you, yourself, on that day go, following orders from the president of the SDS Bosanski Samac, Mr. Sulejman Tihic, to the garrison in Brcko?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I say again: I was not following orders of any kind. We had just had a meeting and we condemned this, and I did go to Brcko to say that the SDA party was not behind what was happening and that we would do everything in our power to remove them. And that's what happened, they were removed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you go to Brcko at your own initiative or was it the result of a decision made by an organ, perhaps the Crisis Staff of the SDA, or some other body perhaps?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, let me say that it might have been the Crisis Staff. Let's say that, that I didn't go on my own, but we decided that it was necessary to go to Brcko and to tell the truth about everything, as far as that was possible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you agree with me that the stated barricades were erected and positioned by Mr. Alija Fitozovic, the commander of your armed unit?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say. I didn't see it. I was sleeping that night, and in the morning when I got up, I heard about this and then saw it. But I can't agree with you there, because I don't know that this was done by an individual. There were probably a few -- group of people who had got together, or perhaps somebody from the party might have been involved, but I don't have any details about that incident at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Izetbegovic, at one of the meetings of the municipal board of the SDA party, did you discuss the question of erecting barricades and responsibilities of the participants in those barricades?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we did condemn it, and we realised that this had been done to our detriment largely. Now, what actually happened, we're not clear today, but each of us, individually and personally, can think about that, and when somebody asks me, I know roughly what had happened. But it wasn't an easy matter. We were bombed from -- bombarded from all sides, with various accusations hurled at us, false accusations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. Do you agree with me that there are three entrance points into the town of Samac?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Shall I enumerate them? I don't know. Let me see. One, two, three -- yes, three.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May the map, Exhibit P9, be shown to Mr. Izetbegovic once again, and perhaps he can point out those three entrances into town.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Before he does that, I want to ask counsel: Are these entrances marked by towns? Do they appear on the map as towns, or would we need the witness to use a pen or some coloured instrument to actually cross them?

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness can mark this with a marker pen. He can mark the entrances. That ought not to represent a problem. I just don't know whether Mr. Izetbegovic's sight is good enough for him to be able to see these points.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: That's why I asked if it's through particular towns, in which case there would be no need for marking them. If you say they went through Amsterdam, for instance, there's no need for us to mark it on the map if Amsterdam is shown on the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, they are entrance points into town from three directions. They go from the rural settlement areas, from the villages, and then you get into town. So he will be able to indicate the directions coming into town.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. In which case, then he should mark them.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Izetbegovic, can you mark the entrance into the town of Samac from the direction of Modrica.

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Let me see the map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Can the witness be shown the map, and he should use the marker, what do you call the instrument, because we are using the ELMO. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Because we don't have another copy for marking, so he will use the pointer. Yes, the Prosecution. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours pleases, I think we had better be clear about what you're using, because otherwise we might run into problems. This map has been marked, I think. In fact, if you look at the ELMO, you can see a black spot.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: I think this is P9, the one that was marked by Tihic originally.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: And after, we agreed that every time we're going to mark the map, we should either have a fresh map or, alternatively, there's something that goes into the transcript so that the markings now made by Mr. Izetbegovic are clearly distinguished from that black spot which was marked by Mr. Tigic. As far as the Prosecution is concerned, it doesn't matter which method is adopted, so long as we don't have markings that we can't later identify, so that's all I think should be -- either we mark it with something different than a black spot, perhaps a number or something like that, or initials, or we use a new --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Let's see where he points first. Let's see where this witness points with the indicator.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you indicate to us the entrance to the town of Samac from the direction of Modrica or the Crka [phoen] and Pisari villages.

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is it here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Could you now indicate --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... -- with the pointer. By the time we get the English translation, the pointer is off the mark, yes. So can he do that again and leave it for -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Stay there with your pointer. Leave the pointer there.

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: What I want to know is, does it have a name? Does that entrance have a name? No. Okay. So we need it to be marked in a different colour. It will still remain an exhibit for the Prosecution, but marked as the transcript will show. MR. DI FAZIO: I've got a pink marking pen if that would be of any assistance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Izetbegovic, would you mark all those entrances with the magic marker you have in your hand now, which is pink in colour, the first first.

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You want the junction near your house?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: If that is the correct position, why not?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you show us the entrance now from Orasje, or rather, the village of Tisina.

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. So when it goes back on the ELMO, then he can explain this one is near whatever town so that we all get it clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you now indicate, please, Mr. Izetbegovic, the entrance from the village of Prud into the town of Samac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: And can we have it marked "1" beside the circle, in pink.

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks] MR. DI FAZIO: I think it's a different entrance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: What? MR. DI FAZIO: I'm sorry, Your Honours. I think it's a different entrance from the other two--

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The ones -- MR. DI FAZIO: -- from the other two that were marked, so ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Because I understood counsel to have asked the witness to mark all the entrances. MR. DI FAZIO: No. I think now we're getting a third one marked, I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Okay. All right.

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I should now like to ask you to indicate to us the places, the entrances to town where the barricades had been set up, at which points.

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see those barricades at all. All I know is that in this part -- but I didn't see any of them. I just know that what happened was in this part, moving towards the bridge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Now, before we leave that, for purposes of clarification, because there are three points, can we have "1," "2," "3," and describe the names, if they have any. Can we have that again marked on the spots with the pink marker so that we have the same colour for this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's like this: We can put the Ciglana entrance, Ciglana --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: That's number 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- as you, Witness, say, next to my house. That's number 1. Then number 2 can be the Uzarija entrance; and entrance number 3, the entrance from the direction of the village of Prud.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you agree with me, Mr. Izetbegovic, that the town was not blocked with barricades from the number 3 entrance, moving from the direction of Prud village?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. All I know is that the barricades were at number 2, and when I returned from Brcko, there was nothing, and I didn't see anything, even when I went there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: May we agree with the following fact: that entrance number 3 from Prud village, which was a Croatian village, was free?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was always free, even on the day when --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Was entrance possible for citizens, for the townsfolk from the Serbian villages of Pisari and Skaric, to go into town via the number 1 Ciglana entrance?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't give you the details. I don't know, quite simply. I didn't take part.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. You don't know. That's fine. That's fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can we have the witness complete his answer regarding the entrance number 3 from Prud village? He said, "It was always free, even on the day when --" He didn't complete. Can he complete the answer, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When it began happening, when what happened began happening --

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us the date, please?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, between the 16th and 17th. That's what I was saying, when that happened.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: May we agree that the barricades were erected when this was ordered by the leadership of the Democratic Action Party?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we cannot.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who issued the order for the erection of the barricades?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that either.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know how the barricades were dismantled?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've told you umpteen times that I never saw them, and when I returned, there was nothing there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: May we agree with the fact that the representatives of the JNA said that they would not intervene because of the barricade erection, that that was not under their competencies?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They didn't tell me that when I was there, to see Lieutenant Colonel Nikolic, and with the gentleman inspector -- this is what he said. He received me very nicely. He gave me a cup of coffee. I found them in a completely mobile state. And he said, "Had you not come, we would have started out with our tanks, because they were ready," and thank God that I went when I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Izetbegovic, do you know the following fact: that all the armed formations were placed on the alert of the Croatian Defence Council in Samac municipality?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that. I had no insight at all into their organisation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Izetbegovic, your son's name is Adis Izetbegovic; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I should like to warn you not to mention my son here. I will not speak about my children here. If necessary, I will talk about that with the Trial Chamber separately.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I wish to ask something in that connection. I don't see why your reaction was what it was. I just asked your son's name, whether that was your son's name.

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had no reaction whatsoever. I remained calm. But please don't touch my family. They have suffered enough, Mr. Pisarevic, from your acts in peacetime as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. I withdraw that question. I won't ask you that. Can I ask you this, then: Pasaga Tihic, is he your daughter's husband?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Once again, please refrain from mentioning my family members.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you. Let us now move on to a different area which has to do with the 4th Detachment. And may I propose that we leave that topic for tomorrow, because I see that our time is up, rather than start it now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. And I would like to know how much more time you need to complete your cross-examination, Mr. Pisarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I need 30 minutes at the most.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, could I ask you to perhaps direct that question to remaining Defence counsel, or perhaps I -- yes, if you could, because we have, of course, witnesses who are ready to go and we'd like to be able to have an idea of how long tasks that the Prosecution needs to attend to -- how much time we'll have to attend to those tasks, and secondly, when we could be expected, at least vaguely, to call them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: Defence counsel may be in a position to let us know now if their cross-examinations are going to be short or lengthy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. I think we need a rough estimate, as I'm sure the counsel know the problems we -- the Tribunal normally has with witnesses, retaining witnesses or bringing them over, and things like that. So since you said half an hour, can I have an indication from counsel for Mr. Tadic roughly how long he thinks he will take?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thirty-five to forty minutes maximum.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: One hour, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Madam President, it depends on the, I would say, way of answering, the witness. If the witness will be cooperative, as he was with the Prosecutor, then I can say around one hour would be enough. If the witness will try to avoid answers, to have - I don't know - problem of understanding, then, believe me, I cannot say for precise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I kindly ask you to understand my position. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. I hope that's helpful to the Prosecution. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: We shall rise and continue tomorrow morning at 0930 hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
